result.verdict: Approve with changes, pending one check. The three references mostly match the audits: setter scope and return values, named-only export, cross-runtime MN0030/MN0031 rules, the synchronous renderer→attachElContent flow, the collection payload shapes and borrowed vs owned state. One isolation claim is not backed by the evidence and must be checked before merge. The rest are corrections, gaps and trims. The TextDom example is proportionate and adds no helper just to make the docs correct. The prose mostly avoids overpromising typing or validation.
blockingIssues: runtime.md says each `createMarionette()` starts from copied native defaults 'even after configuring the default family', and that changing one family's slots does not affect another. The audit only shows copies of the Dom, Data and State providers and a restored renderer. It never says the factory gives its classes their own `EventDelegator` (View, CollectionView and Behavior). Each runtime class extends the matching root class. If the runtime classes have no delegator of their own, a later root `setEventDelegator()` (or `View.setEventDelegator`) leaks into every isolated runtime. Check `src/create-marionette.ts` and add an installed assertion: create a runtime, then call root `setEventDelegator`, then confirm the runtime View/Behavior still use the native delegator. Otherwise narrow the isolation claim to the slots that are actually copied.
risks: runtime.md says setters change 'not an instance's already-created element, cached data, or installed subscriptions', which suggests live instances are unaffected. The audit says existing instances that inherit the slot pick up parent changes on their next call. Reconfiguring after construction can therefore mix providers on one live View (e.g. native innerHTML content followed by a Lit `setContents`). State this explicitly.

`monitorViewEvents: false` also turns off `notifyAttach`/`notifyDetach`. With the Lit adapter, that breaks directive connected/disconnected state. The DOM page should link that consequence to integrations that need these notifications.

A synchronous initial `observeCollection` notification crashes with an unhelpful TypeError (`ownerDocument`) instead of an MN diagnostic. The docs record this as a provider obligation. It is also a runtime robustness bug (product bug, not a docs bug) and should be tracked as a decision item in coverage/plan, not only in the audit.

The runtime row is marked 'Audited' while the `monitorViewEvents` export only links to View lifecycle docs. If that page covers the option rather than the standalone function `monitorViewEvents(view)`, the export has no documented contract. It should be classified explicitly or listed as a gap alongside `MarionetteError`.

The source audits ran against an uncommitted working tree (baseline diff hash in coverage.md). The results page does not confirm the hash was rechecked after the audits, so evidence could drift from the source before merge.
incorrectAssumptions: data-providers.md ('Keep source events separate…') says the native data adapter 'forwards collection add/remove/reset/reorder events'. Per the audit, it translates Collection `update` (carrying `changes`), `reset` and `sort`. It does not forward add/remove events one by one. This contradicts the correct 'Native data integration' section on the same page; reword it to match.

runtime.md's scope table implies every class has every static setter. Per the audit, only the classes listed in a row have that static setter (e.g. there is no `Region.setDataApi`, `Application.setDomApi` or `Region.setStateApi`). Say this explicitly.
The native `StateApi.disposeOwned` bullet leaves out that destroying an owned native Collection does not destroy its Models. Readers may assume a cascading dispose.
The renderer section omits that falsy serialized data is replaced with `{}` before the renderer is called. A custom renderer author depends on this.
The Reset row says 'rebuild' but does not say that all existing children are destroyed even when model identities are retained. State it, because it matters for child-owned resources.
missingTests: Installed test: root `setEventDelegator` (and a root `View.setEventDelegator` class call) made after `createMarionette()` must not change the runtime View/CollectionView/Behavior delegator. Symmetric test: a runtime `setEventDelegator` must not change root classes.
Installed test: root `setRenderer` made after `createMarionette()` does not change the runtime renderer. This confirms that 'restores native renderer' means an own slot, not a one-time copy.
Test showing that a live instance inheriting a slot uses the new provider on its next render after a parent setter call. This locks down the corrected wording.
Test that `monitorViewEvents: false` suppresses `notifyAttach`/`notifyDetach` (documented, but no listed test covers it directly).

The 'no initial notification' rule rests only on a temporary probe. Add either a repository test that locks the current failure or a tracked item to turn it into a diagnostic, so the documented obligation does not drift silently.
Fix the test bug in the `test/types/dom.mts` comment: it claims the runtime setter rejects null, but the audit says the setter does no validation.
simplifications: Remove the duplicate 'no runtime EventDelegator/Renderer value' statement from either runtime.md or the dom-providers TypeScript section; keep one canonical copy.
Drop 'including equal NaN keys' and the DocumentFragment/NodeListOf detail on the native `findEl` signature. These are implementation trivia, not author guidance.
In data-providers.md, fold the 'native data adapter forwards…' sentence into the Native data integration section rather than restating it with different wording.

Include the audit's short warning against reporting the same mutation as both a same-object `updated` pair and a model event (double rerender). It is cheaper than readers finding the problem themselves.
nextSteps: Check `createMarionette` for an EventDelegator slot of its own. Either add the installed isolation assertion or correct the isolation prose in runtime.md.

Apply the wording fixes: native adapter event translation, which classes have static setters, live-instance behavior after reconfiguration, and falsy data becoming `{}`. Also cover owned Collection disposal not cascading to Models, and reset destroying all children.
Classify the standalone `monitorViewEvents` export in coverage.md (documented link or gap).
Record the synchronous-initial-notification TypeError as a runtime decision item, and fix the misleading `dom.mts` comment.
Recheck the source diff hash, rerun `reference-contracts` and `reference-examples`, then record this review's disposition in runtime-provider-results.md.
